- The UI must never lie: show 'Saved'/'Deleted'/'Sent'/'Synced'/'Unlocked' ONLY after it truly happened — never before, never unconditionally, never a success animation regardless of the real result.
- No sample/placeholder data shown as if it were the user's real data. When there's no real data yet, show an honest empty state, not fabricated stats.
- Give every data-driven screen an EXPLICIT state model (an enum like idle/loading/loaded/empty/failed) — not a pile of loose isLoading/hasError/showEmpty booleans that can form impossible combinations.
- Adaptive layout: reflow, wrap, or scroll — never clip. No hardcoded screen-level frames. Set a sensible minimum window size on macOS. Honor Dynamic Type and dark mode (test long text and large text).
- NEVER let text or controls OVERLAP or collide. Labels must not sit on top of values; two values must not stack into each other. When you place elements by a data value (along a timeline/axis/gradient, e.g. event times on a chart), you MUST guarantee a minimum gap and de-clutter — when two would collide (values close together, or a high-latitude day with events bunched up), offset, group, collapse, or drop a label rather than draw one over another. A screen where text overlaps is a broken screen, full stop.
- Persist real data (must survive relaunch) and preserve the user's input across failures — a failed save must not wipe the form.
- Prevent duplicate submissions (disable the trigger while it's in flight). Treat user cancellation as a normal outcome, NOT an error.
- Accessibility is part of the build, not a cleanup pass: accessible labels on icon-only buttons, status conveyed by more than color, keyboard-navigable.
- Validate real and adversarial input; never surface raw internal errors, stack traces, file paths, or tokens to the user.
- In your wrap-up, HONESTLY name anything left as a placeholder, mock, or unfinished path — never claim a feature is done on the basis of it compiling.
